The figures, forecasts and key figures are calculations based on what you enter and on public data such as market prices, which can be delayed or wrong. The little dashed line in a budget bar: how much of the budget you could have spent by today if you spread it evenly over the month — about 13% on the 4th, half on the 15th. Orange: you've spent more than that so far. Not a problem by itself — a quieter few days bring you back on pace. Fixed costs don't get one: they're paid at once.
The market moves your investments without you doing anything. Up: more equity. Down: less.

The middle ring is a daily goal: a day counts when what you spent that day stays under what you earned that day. Your salary and fixed costs count a day's worth each day, so rent on the 1st and pay on the 25th don't skew it; other spending and income count on their own day. The ring is full when 80% of the month's days stayed under your income — 24 of 30. In the calendar, a day's green ring is full when that day stayed under.
